0__freddie__0: At the depot, Wendel "Mole" Freddie had practised answering to his name. At R-F14, the first person to call it only wanted help with a crate.
Wendel "Mole" Freddie was in the first hundred. The old hands in R-F14 call them 'the early birds', and not always kindly.
The machine gunners took Wendel "Mole" Freddie in on a wet morning in R-F14. By noon he had learned the first rule of the job, and by evening the second.
A bullet found Wendel "Mole" Freddie at R-F14, high in the shoulder. He went down hard and stayed down. Shot by Ulrich Gpt of the Concord (@ghai.gpt).
Verdel Ridge is lost. Wendel "Mole" Freddie heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.

A bed came free in the hospital dugout, and Wendel "Mole" Freddie was carried in at last. Wendel "Mole" Freddie bought War Bonds for the front. The quartermaster pinned the ribbon on personally: 'The front remembers who kept it fed.'
There was never a bed for Wendel "Mole" Freddie, so the medics brought the hospital to him. Three days on a stretcher, and he walked back to R-F14 on his own feet.

Wendel "Mole" Freddie lent Henrik Sedlomancz a pencil. It came back wrapped in a scrap of paper that said 'One good turn'. The Hegemony took Hill 304, and the orders at R-F14 changed before the cheering ended. Wendel "Mole" Freddie shouldered another load.
A flare lit the Hanging Bridge like noon. Wendel "Mole" Freddie counted the seconds until darkness: eleven.

Wendel "Mole" Freddie fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Felix Kagr, gravely wounded. Nobody nearby said anything. A bullet clipped Wendel "Mole" Freddie's helmet at R-F14 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Gideon Actioncam of the Concord (@actioncam3000).
Back on the fire step at R-F14. Wendel "Mole" Freddie says the wound itches, which the medics say is a good sign.

Two men fed the belt while Wendel "Mole" Freddie held the gun steady on the enemy parapet. When they stopped, Florian "Doc" Guyy was grazed. Wendel "Mole" Freddie was found at the bottom of the trench at R-F14, hit in the head, helmet split open. He is breathing in short, loud gasps. Shot by Viktor Detroit of the Concord (@major_detroit313). Wendel "Mole" Freddie was killed at R-F14 while passing a message along the trench. He never finished the sentence. Shot by Viktor Detroit of the Concord (@major_detroit313).

The papers connected Dorian "Parson" Freddie to Wendel "Mole" Freddie. The men took longer to learn Dorian "Parson" Freddie's own habits, but they made the effort. Dorian "Parson" Freddie received the First Wave ribbon. He checked the stitching twice before putting the tunic back on. After what happened at the Drowned Farm, Dorian "Parson" Freddie asked to serve as a machine gunner. Nobody argued.

Dorian "Parson" Freddie was on watch at R-F14 when the night raid hit. The men found Dorian "Parson" Freddie at dawn by the dugout door. Killed in the night raid by Norbert Alsnafe of the Concord (@alsnafe7490).

A letter came with Karel Freddie: "I am Dorian "Parson" Freddie's brother. I have come to finish what he started." Nobody had the heart to tell him it never finishes. The First Wave ribbon marked Karel Freddie as an early volunteer. At R-F14, a newcomer asked what those first days had been like.
_z2xman3_: The old hands of S-R6 have been here since Day 1. Jakub "Mole" Xman has been here since Day 9. In a trench, that difference already feels like years.
From Blackwater Canal the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Jakub "Mole" Xman wrote to an old neighbor who promised to keep his garden alive that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'
aggiomarco: Lucien Aggiomarco was a tailor in Coldwater until the posters went up. He came to S-R9 with a tin of tobacco, and within a day the whole squad knew that he draws portraits of the men in the margins of letters.
Blackwater Canal fell to the Hegemony at dusk. Lucien Aggiomarco helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
caboose_flyer1280102938392: Tobias Flyer reached R-C4 expecting a speech. The welcome consisted of a mug, a space on a bench and directions to the latrine.

The enemy post had been quiet all morning. Tobias Flyer waited for that to change. When it did, Hugo "Brick" Reiddemars was grazed. News that the Hegemony had taken Blackwater Canal reached Tobias Flyer during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
eduard._.eddie: Oskar Eddie was a medical student in Belmonte until the posters went up. He came to R-F10 with a tin whistle, and within a day the whole bay knew that he tells terrible jokes.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Oskar Eddie was number 42. He still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
Oskar Eddie reported for duty as a stretcher bearer. The new kit was heavier than the explanation of how to use it.
A muddy dog crawled into R-F10 through the wire. Oskar Eddie gave it half his bread. It has not left his side since. The men call it Lump.

The cook asked for an honest opinion. Oskar Eddie asked whether second helpings depended on the answer. Word came down the line: Verdel Ridge is ours. Oskar Eddie shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Oskar Eddie stretched a scrap of canvas over the letters. Everything else could get wet first.
Lump has learned to carry messages in a tin on its collar. Oskar Eddie is very proud. Lump is mainly proud of the biscuits.

Oskar Eddie raised his head for a heartbeat too long at R-F10. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Pavel "Crow" Hayden of the Hegemony (@hayden.dt). From Hill 304 the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Oskar Eddie wrote to a girl from the dance hall, maybe that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'
The medics cleaned Oskar Eddie's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at R-F10.
A patient apologized for bleeding on Oskar Eddie's sleeve. He told the patient to concentrate on staying awake.
Somebody hung a doorbell on the next dugout. Oskar Eddie went to look. It was a spoon tied to an empty tin.
Oskar Eddie wrote a song about Hill 304. Yann "Lucky" Lettersabcd wrote a second verse. The squad has banned the third.
Oskar Eddie was on watch at R-F10 when the night raid hit. The men found Oskar Eddie at dawn by the dugout door. Killed in the night raid by Yann "Saint" Ain of the Hegemony (@mount.ain220).

Felix "Brick" Eddie put a tin whistle beside the bunk. Someone who had known Oskar Eddie helped clear the shelf without saying why. Number 42 on the early rolls: Felix "Brick" Eddie. The First Wave ribbon arrived with instructions about where to sew it and no needle.
ghostoftheast: The new machine gunner gave his name as Zeno Ghostoftheas. The corporal looked at his boots, then at the mud, and laughed for the first time in a week.
A lice inspection interrupted a heated argument about politics. Zeno Ghostoftheas pointed out that at least one enemy had been positively identified.
Zeno Ghostoftheas found water collecting beneath the gun's cover. He sketched a small shelter and took the drawing to the stores.
Zeno Ghostoftheas brought sandbags forward and found the damage worse than the message had said. The party went back for another load.
The stores supplied Zeno Ghostoftheas with shorter boards than requested. The gun shelter has become an exercise in joints and bad language.

The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal, and the orders at S-S7 changed before the cheering ended. Zeno Ghostoftheas shouldered another load. A letter from home reached Zeno Ghostoftheas before dusk. Zeno Ghostoftheas read it twice and slept a little easier.
john_goez: Otto Goez told the sergeant he was a tailor. The sergeant said the war needed one of those like it needed a hole in the roof, and put him on sentry.

Otto Goez was cleaning the rifle when a head showed across the wire. Load, aim, fire. Gustav Gsingeis was badly wounded. Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Otto Goez stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
krauser.yuas: Lucien "Brick" Yuas arrived with the Day 10 draft, carrying a stub of a pencil and the news from home, which was old by the time he told it.
localfilipinoboi: The new lieutenant is Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin, once a tailor from Tannenfeld. The corporal asked if a tailor was any use in a trench. Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin said he would find out.
A football came over the parapet from the Concord side with Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin's name scratched on it. Emil Galvanooooo kicked it back. It did not come again.
Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin stretched a scrap of canvas over the letters. Everything else could get wet first.

A bullet clipped Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin's helmet at R-F4 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Gideon Bao of the Hegemony (@d4rth_bao). The sergeant read out the order: Hill 304 has fallen, hold the line. Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.
The medics cleaned Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at R-F4.
Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin raised his head for a heartbeat too long at R-F4. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Jonas Solyommadar of the Hegemony (@solyommadar11).

Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin was hit in the foot through his boot at R-F4. The boot had to be cut off. He asked them to save the other one. Shot by Walter "Hollow" Malakaicripp of the Hegemony (@malakaicripps). A single shot at R-F4. Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin sat down against the trench wall as if to rest, and did not get up. Shot by Walter "Hollow" Malakaicripp of the Hegemony (@malakaicripps).
The papers say Casimir "Lucky" Localfilipin. The sergeant says he has his cousin's eyes. Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin's eyes. Nobody in R-F4 argues.

Casimir "Lucky" Localfilipin was hit in the hand while passing a mug along the trench at R-F4. He did not spill a drop. The men are still talking about that. Shot by Wendel Jesus of the Hegemony (@jesus.gr9).

The medic looked at Casimir "Lucky" Localfilipin's wound, sniffed it, and sent him back to R-F4. Clean, said the medic. It is the best word a medic knows. Blackwater Canal is lost. Casimir "Lucky" Localfilipin heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.
mustafa1utku: Nobody saw Jonas Utku arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in R-F16, and a quiet runner under it.

Jonas Utku sharpened a pencil with great care and then could not think what to write. He put the date at the top anyway. Word came down the line: Verdel Ridge is ours. Jonas Utku shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Someone asked Jonas Utku to wake them in ten minutes. He had no watch, so he counted slowly and woke them at what felt like ten.
A supply man offered Jonas Utku a damaged gramophone in exchange for help unloading. He accepted before asking whether there were any records.

Jonas Utku coaxed the gramophone into turning. It plays a march played slightly too slowly, but something knocks once every revolution. A letter from home found Jonas Utku before the night shift. Jonas Utku folded it small and kept it close. Day 6: Hill 304 was lost. Jonas Utku wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
Jonas Utku brushed dried mud off a letter and found one more word under it: 'soon'. He wished the rest of the sentence had survived.
A bullet went through Jonas Utku's sleeve at R-F16 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Shot by Jakub Virajvirxgil of the Hegemony (@virajvirxgill13).
Back on the fire step at R-F16. Jonas Utku says the wound itches, which the medics say is a good sign.
The gramophone stopped knocking after Jonas Utku tightened a screw. The dugout applauded the repair halfway through a march played slightly too slowly, spoiling the best part.

Jonas Utku was on the dawn watch at R-F16 when the Hegemony raiders came. A club, a shout, and Jonas Utku was on the trench floor waiting for the medic. Raider: Jakub "Brick" Ingfan of the Hegemony (@seal.ingfan). The report confirmed that the Hegemony held Blackwater Canal. Jonas Utku read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.
noah813768: At the depot, Nils Noah had practised answering to his name. At R-S16, the first person to call it only wanted help with a crate.
Nils Noah drew the street leading to Tannenfeld. There was no room left for the last house, so he turned the page over.

Nils Noah saw a helmet rise behind the enemy sandbags at R-S16 and fired once. Isidor Jrca was grazed. After the loss of Blackwater Canal, Nils Noah helped stack spare sandbags at R-S16. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
otroserhumanoo: Viktor Otroserhuman, a medical student from Lindenbruck, was sent forward on Day 9 to fill a gap in R-R14. The gap had a name once. Nobody says it.
The Hegemony flag went up over Blackwater Canal. Viktor Otroserhuman did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.
rockytheautistic: Leopold Rockytheauti was a coal miner in Oakmere until the posters went up. He came to R-R5 with his brother's pocket watch, and within a day the whole squad knew that he is always the first one awake.

A bullet hit the sandbag next to Leopold Rockytheauti's ear at R-R5 and sprayed his face with grit and blood. A scratch, the medic said, and a lucky one. Shot by Walter "Hollow" Malakaicripp of the Hegemony (@malakaicripps). Day 10: Blackwater Canal was lost. Leopold Rockytheauti wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
shimmapaul: Nobody asked Roland "Tin" Shimmapaul why he came. Nobody in Q-S11 asks that. He was handed a spade before he was handed a rifle.

Roland "Tin" Shimmapaul has fired hundreds of rounds into the dark. Today one of them found someone: Viktor "Crow" Borgia, grazed. The Hegemony hold Blackwater Canal now, and they can see straight into Q-S11. Roland "Tin" Shimmapaul has learned to walk bent double.
sleetius_maximus: They issued Zeno "Shadow" Maximus a rifle, a spade and a number. He kept a dented harmonica in his breast pocket, where the shrapnel would have to go through it first.
Zeno "Shadow" Maximus answered the first call, number 85 on the rolls. Somebody chalked the number on his helmet. It has not washed off yet.
Zeno "Shadow" Maximus agreed to sit for a portrait drawn by a man with a piece of charcoal. The first result made him look twice his age.

The listening post reported scraping beyond the wire. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus waited through an hour of it before a loose stake was found. News that the Concord had taken Verdel Ridge reached Zeno "Shadow" Maximus during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
A clear shot from S-F9. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus grazed Arno Toastyy and slid back down below the parapet.

The artist tried again while Zeno "Shadow" Maximus read a letter. The new portrait was better, though the ears became the subject of discussion. Mail came up the line with a letter for Zeno "Shadow" Maximus. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Zeno "Shadow" Maximus crawled out with the wiring party. When a flare went up, he lay still and counted to ten. The wire at S-F9 holds again. The report confirmed that the Hegemony held Hill 304. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.

Dawn watch. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton, badly wounded. Mail came up the line with a letter for Zeno "Shadow" Maximus. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

A single shot from across the wire hit Zeno "Shadow" Maximus in the thigh at S-F9. He crawled the last yards on his elbows. Shot by Dietrich Wolfmananton of the Hegemony (@wolfmanantony). Mail came up the line with a letter for Zeno "Shadow" Maximus. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Zeno "Shadow" Maximus reached the hospital dugout after a long wait. The surgeon took one look at the wound and went to wash up. Mail came up the line with a letter for Zeno "Shadow" Maximus. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Another quiet day in the ward for Zeno "Shadow" Maximus. He counted the cracks in the ceiling and got to forty-one. Mail came up the line with a letter for Zeno "Shadow" Maximus. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Zeno "Shadow" Maximus never saw the inside of the aid post. The medics changed his dressings on the stretcher until the wound closed. He is back on the line. Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores. Mail came up the line with a letter for Zeno "Shadow" Maximus. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
the_slive: The sergeant gave Casimir Slive a dead man's blanket and a living man's job. That is how replacements start, on Day 9 or any other. Casimir Slive's transfer to the role of stretcher bearer was approved. The quartermaster wanted every borrowed item back before issuing anything else.

The Hegemony flag went up over Blackwater Canal. Casimir Slive did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again. A letter from home reached Casimir Slive before dusk. Casimir Slive read it twice and slept a little easier.
valsteinne: The sergeant gave Roland Valsteinne a dead man's blanket and a living man's job. That is how replacements start, on Day 8 or any other.
Roland Valsteinne found a photograph in the mud of no man's land: a woman in a white dress, and a name on the back that is not from his side of the wire.

A bullet hit the sandbag next to Roland Valsteinne's ear at S-S14 and sprayed his face with grit and blood. A scratch, the medic said, and a lucky one. Shot by Otto "Hollow" Crabbithesec of the Concord (@crabbithesecond). Blackwater Canal fell to the Hegemony at dusk. Roland Valsteinne helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
voktor__crack: Edmund Crack was a clockmaker in Rosenau until the posters went up. He came to R-F8 with a photograph gone soft at the edges, and within a day the whole bay knew that he whistles the same four notes over and over.
Day 3. The Concord took Verdel Ridge. From the heights Edmund Crack could see the whole Hegemony line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.
Part of the parapet collapsed near Edmund Crack. Repairs started as soon as the dust settled, with one man on watch while the rest worked.
Edmund Crack wrote a letter home. He wrote about the weather. He did not write about the rats.

Edmund Crack fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Marek Izu, grazed. Nobody nearby said anything. Hill 304 is lost. Edmund Crack heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.
A bullet went through Edmund Crack's sleeve at R-F8 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Shot by Benedikt Ngaihte of the Hegemony (@mng.ngaihte).
Edmund Crack no longer winces when he lifts his rifle. The medic signed him off with a grunt.
Edmund Crack took stock of his pockets: string, crumbs, a pencil and no sign of the button he was looking for.
Edmund Crack reached up to fix a sandbag at R-F8 and a bullet took the skin off two knuckles. The sandbag got fixed anyway. Shot by Felix Zulfi of the Hegemony (@rayan.zulfi).

Back on the fire step at R-F8. Edmund Crack says the wound itches, which the medics say is a good sign. From Blackwater Canal the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Edmund Crack wrote to his mother, who writes every Sunday that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'
zannwaffen_: Day 9: Yann Zannwaffen reached R-C10 with a full packet of cigarettes. Learning everyone's name proved remarkably easy.
The Hegemony secured Blackwater Canal. Yann Zannwaffen helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that he had heard correctly.
